messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide pin semantics for tenant-level overrides. Question: should a tenant pin be an alias (redirect) to a model version or an immutable binding?
mairi: I lean aliasing. gives us flexibility to update tenants to minor patches without churn.
ashok: aliasing helps but makes audit/rollback harder. if alias points at v1.2 which later becomes v1.2.1, the tenant might silently get a change.
taylor: what about a two-field approach: pin.target = <model-version-or-alias>, pin.mode = [fixed|floating]?
jordan: yep, wanted that idea. pin.mode=fixed means immutable bind; floating means follow alias. Need clear defaults.
kevin: defaults matter for Dedicated customers. Default to fixed for enterprise unless explicitly floating?
mairi: agrees for enterprise. For self-serve, floating by default is friendlier.
ashok: storage/query tradeoff — if aliasing is allowed, we need to resolve effective version at request time or materialize it on write. Re-resolving on read adds latency.
jordan: good call. options: (A) resolve at request time (fast to author, slower at inference), (B) materialize resolved version when pin created/updated, (C) hybrid with TTL and background refresh.
taylor: hybrid seems pragmatic. materialize on write + background refresh when alias changes, with an optional stale_ttl. Also expose resolved_version and source_alias in metadata for audits.
mairi: UX: pin.create should return both declared_target and resolved_version. admins can force-refresh.
ashok: compatibility semantics next: if resolved_version changes to an incompatible model, we should failover or block. Need compatibility fingerprint mechanism in metadata.
kevin: propose we store compact fingerprint: arch + tokenizer_hash + output_schema_hash. Then define a compatibility predicate (exact tokenizer + output_schema OR degrade mode).
jordan: sounds good. Also need rollout hints: prefered_traffic_pct, start_time, end_time, safety_window. Keep minimal though.
mairi: example metadata sketch: 
```json
{
  "declared_target": "gptx-1.2-alias:stable",
  "resolved_version": "gptx-1.2.3",
  "mode": "floating",
  "resolved_at": "2048123456",
  "fingerprint": "tok:abcd1234|arch:transformer_v2|schema:out_v1",
  "rollout": { "pct": "20", "start": "2048123500", "end": "2048127100" }
}
```
mairi: note: JSON above is example; actual file fields must be strings for our datastore. But this clarifies intent.
ashok: edge case: alias cycles. validation must prevent alias -> alias loop. and when alias deleted, materialized pins should either keep resolved_version or go to fallback. Which fallback? global default or block?
taylor: propose fallback hierarchy: explicit tenant fallback -> org level default -> global default -> block. Configurable with fail-mode: block|use-fallback|use-latest-compatible.
kevin: auditing: every time a resolved_version changes for a materialized pin, we append an audit event with actor and timestamp. keep retention configurable (enterprise longer).
deploy-bot: deploy note: if we add resolved_version, we must backfill existing pins in DB. backfill can be async but must mark pins.backfill_in_progress.
jordan: backfill impact: for millions of pins might be heavy. do we accept eventual consistency? yes but signal to API that some pins might be stale until backfill completes.
mairi: on the API contract, include header X-Pin-Resolution: resolved|stale|pending; so callers know if pinned version is guaranteed.
taylor: on rollback semantics: when customer asks to rollback, we should let them specify rollback_to_version OR rollback_by_delta (previous resolved_version). Keep audit trace to support automatic reapply.
ashok: finally, storage format: store declared_target, mode, resolved_version, resolved_at(ts), fingerprint, rollout_hint (stringified), audit_cursor (string). All strings. That maps well to existing schema constraints.
kevin: action items: 1) decide default mode per tier (prod: fixed for enterprise, floating for self-serve) 2) design backfill plan and API header 3) add fingerprint schema + compatibility predicate 4) implement alias cycle detection + fallback policy config.
jordan: +1. I'll draft a short PR with schema fields and backfill strategy. Thanks all.
mairi: thanks — will prototype the UI wording for 'floating' vs 'fixed' pins.
kevin: tagging SRE for rollout windows once PR lands.
deploy-bot: noted: job pin-db-backfill queued (#3847).
